items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I'm sitting at the window and I lean out and just said to women going to work, 'Hi, Sue.'

ctx.x: Yeah, we were in the Dunbar. We were living there. So the hotel got to shaking one morning, early. I was downstairs in the shooting gallery, because (inaudible) down there getting an eye-opener. Man, one of them light tremors -- one of them heavy tremors. Ray Nance got downstairs in the lobby of this hotel with only his shorts on. I said, "Man, where are you going?" He said, "Man, the world's coming to an end." I said, "Man, it's okay." Had to take a lot of people to talk to him, he was so scared. But I'm…

So we used to go out, the studio would send a driver for us. Come out -- because that's a long ways out to Hollywood from Central Avenue. We had to go out early. So we were riding around, riding around. And you know, the car stopped -- the bus stops in California, they sit on the side. So we were riding along and I'm sitting at the window and I lean out and just said to women going to work, "Hi, Sue."
